the micronucleus assay is a useful test for radiation sensitivity and may have the potential to identify a high frequency of cases predisposed to breast cancer.

the identification of genetic factors that influence the risk of breast cancer.
the identification of individuals who may be at high risk of developing breast cancer and the development of tests for the detection of such predisposed individuals.

the HDR assay for radiation-induced micronucleus formation in G0 lymphocyte cultures is a simple and reproducible assay, which identifies a substantial number of breast cancer patients as being highly radiosensitive.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a high frequency of breast cancer patients showing elevated radiosensitivity, and we have developed a simple, rapid assay that may have clinical utility.
the majority of breast cancers are not due to the BRCA1 or BRCA2 genes, but rather to a number of low penetrance, high frequency genes, which may be detected by radiation-induced micronucleus assays.

The main takeaway from our work is that
there may be a genetic predisposition to breast cancer that is not related to BRCA1 or BRCA2, and that the G2 assay and the micronucleus assay are useful tools for identifying such predisposition.
